01 · Before us

How content was being made in March.

Hooks

Written, not researched

Hooks were pulled out of the script after it was written. One per video, sometimes two. Nothing was tested against anything.

Research

Trend-watching

Scrolling for trending audio and fonts. No outlier study, no record of what had already worked in the category.

Production

The editor guessed

Script and hook, nothing else. No shot list, no timing, no frame direction. A third of output was repurposed from YouTube.

There was no funnel. Asked directly about top and middle of funnel in March, there was no split in use.

02 · The system we built

The production line we put in place.

Every reel now runs the same route. Before us, only the last two steps existed.

ResearchPlanHooksScriptComplianceShootEditTrial & post
What changed
Was
  • Hook written off a pain-point list
  • One hook, never tested
  • Editor given creative freedom
Now
  • Hooks sourced from proven performers
  • Three to four hooks, tested as trials
  • Editor and filming instructions written in
Why
  • The hook decides the video
  • The winner is chosen by data
  • Half of edit time went on hunting assets

03 · What we overcame

The delay was never the writing.

In June we traced it properly. Fifteen scripts went out on the 1st and came back written by the 4th. The two weeks then disappeared into shooting and edit.

Assumed causeScripting

The visible step, so the one everyone looked at first.

→
Actual causeShoot & edit

Fixed by adding a dedicated shooter and batching shoot days.

Naming the right bottleneck is why July moved. Fixing scripting would have changed nothing.
09 / 25
03 · Compliance

The biggest problem we hit, and it cost us live posts.

The post

An RBI licence reel

The opening line stated, as fact, that you no longer needed to repay your loan.

The objection

It was not true

Expert Panel stops illegal harassment. Recovery is the lender’s legal right. That claim reaches a regulator.

The cost

Posts pulled after going live

Three to four from the first batch, two to three archived later. One had already crossed 160,000 views.

The reach and the risk came from the same sentence. That is what made it hard to fix.
10 / 25
03 · Compliance

What we built so it stopped happening.

The written standard
  • A checklist every video runs before it goes out
  • Five hard prohibitions, shared with the whole team
  • Never guarantee a score recovery or a timeline
  • Never name the lender
The craft fix
  • Frame the claim as true-or-false, not as a statement
  • Or state the myth, then debunk it
  • Carry the question mark in the on-screen text, so the spoken hook keeps its pull
The process fix
  • Approval moved to the scripting stage
  • Topics approved before a script is written
  • A four-stage approval chain client-side
  • Legal review added from July

04 · How we trained the team

The clearest example is the scripting itself.

In March

Long and unstructured

No word limit. Editor notes mixed into spoken lines. Hooks written cold. The full subject crammed into one reel.

What we taught

A format, and the reasons

130 to 150 words. Editor notes in their own layer. Three genuinely different hooks. One point per reel. Text hooks of four to six words.

Within two weeks

Applied unprompted

A documents list was cut to three items without being asked, because more would have pushed the script past the word limit.

That is the difference between delivery and capability. One of them survives us leaving the room.

Carousels buy impressions. Reels buy followers.

Carousel views to reach2.51x
Reel views to reach1.32x
Follows from 6 carousels3

A 2.51 ratio means the same people are seeing it repeatedly. Carousels re-serve the existing audience. They do not find new one.

06 · Retention

Skip rate is the single strongest predictor of reach.

Most viewers decide inside three seconds. The ones who stay are the entire audience.

Win the first three seconds and everything else follows. Nothing else in this dataset correlates half as strongly.

07 · Topics

Recovery-agent harassment is our repeatable winner.

Worked
  • Recovery agent harassment, three separate reels at 41,306 / 33,060 / 26,657
  • Rebuild CIBIL, consistent across three attempts
  • Legal notice explained
  • EMI default consequences
Did not
  • Loan settlement explained
  • Minimum payment maths
  • CIBIL myth-busters
  • NBFC licence cancellation
The pattern
  • A specific situation beats a general topic
  • Something at stake right now beats education
  • Borrower Rights carries every breakout
  • Neutral how-to plateaus regardless of quality
22 / 25
05 · Formats

We ran 58 hook tests. Most could not be read.

Every reel ships as multiple unlisted variations to test the hook before the winner goes out. The programme ran, but the samples were too small to separate good hooks from noise.

What ran
  • 58 variations across 30 batches
  • Median 188 views per variation
  • Winning position split evenly: H1 five, H2 four, H3 twice
  • No positional bias, so the tests were sound
The problem
  • Most spreads were 1.0x to 2.0x
  • On a 250-view sample that is noise
  • Only throttled batches showed a big gap
And some were throttled
  • Variants landing at 0 to 24 views against siblings at 200 plus
  • Reach tracked views 1:1, so they were never delivered
  • Two of eleven tested reels affected
